title: CI/CD DORA Metrics (Real-time)

list.name: allowed_lateness_hours
list.label: Allowed lateness (hours)
list.description: Must match the ALLOWED_LATENESS constants in DeploymentFrequencyOperator.java, DoraOperators.java (CFR_ALLOWED_LATENESS), and PipelineHealthOperator.java — all three are Time.hours(5) = 5h. Update this value by hand if any of those constants change. Not auto-synced.

list.name: deployment_frequency_window_seconds
list.label: Deployment frequency window size (seconds)
list.description: Must match FlinkConfig.DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_WINDOW (currently Time.days(1) = 86400s), which also sizes the live counter's bucket in LiveDeployCounter. Not auto-synced — update by hand if that constant changes.

panels.title: Current Watermark (job-global)
panels.description: The event-time watermark the whole job is currently at (WatermarkReporterOperator). To test truly-late handling: compare THIS value (not your test event's timestamp) against a window's window_alive_until in the panel below. Once this watermark passes that window's window_alive_until, an event timestamped inside that window (still [window_start, window_end) — window_alive_until never changes that range) will route to TRULY_LATE_TAG instead of updating the window.

targets.rawSql: SELECT value AS current_watermark FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'WATERMARK' AND pipeline_id = 'GLOBAL' ORDER BY inserted_at DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Deployment Frequency (deploys/day)
panels.description: Plotted by event time (window_end), not by inserted_at — a fast backlog replay can write results for many different event-time days within the same few real-world minutes, which would otherwise bunch every point onto the same narrow slice of a real-time X-axis regardless of which simulated day it actually describes. This intentionally has no dashboard time-range filter, since 'window_end' and the picker's 'last 6 hours' are different clocks (event time vs wall-clock time).

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS "time", value, pipeline_id AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY' ORDER BY window_end_ms

panels.title: Lead Time for Changes (minutes)
panels.description: Plotted by event time (window_end — the DEPLOY_SUCCESS timestamp for that commit), not inserted_at, for the same reason as Deployment Frequency: a fast backlog replay writes results for many different event-time moments within the same few real-world minutes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS "time", value, pipeline_id AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'LEAD_TIME_FOR_CHANGES' ORDER BY window_end_ms

panels.title: Change Failure Rate (%)
panels.description: The (window close) series is plotted by event time (window_end) rather than inserted_at, same reason as Deployment Frequency — it's a real TumblingEventTimeWindow. The (live) series stays on inserted_at deliberately: CHANGE_FAILURE_RATE_LIVE upserts one row per pipeline under a fixed 1970-01-01 sentinel (see CFR_LIVE_WINDOW_MARKER), so window_end_ms is constant there and useless as an axis — inserted_at is the only real time signal that series has.

targets.rawSql: SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (live)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'CHANGE_FAILURE_RATE_LIVE' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (window close)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'CHANGE_FAILURE_RATE' ORDER BY window_end_ms

panels.title: Mean Time to Recovery (minutes)
panels.description: Plotted by event time (window_end — the BUILD_SUCCESS/recovery timestamp), not inserted_at, same reason as Deployment Frequency: a fast backlog replay writes results for many different event-time moments within the same few real-world minutes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS "time", value, pipeline_id AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'MEAN_TIME_TO_RECOVERY' ORDER BY window_end_ms

panels.title: Pipeline Health Score
panels.description: The (window close) series is plotted by event time (window_end) rather than inserted_at, same reason as Deployment Frequency — it's a real 30-min TumblingEventTimeWindow. The (live) series stays on inserted_at deliberately: PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE_LIVE upserts one row per pipeline under a fixed 1970-01-01 sentinel (see LIVE_WINDOW_MARKER in PipelineHealthOperator), so window_end_ms is constant there and useless as an axis — inserted_at is the only real time signal that series has.

targets.rawSql: SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (live)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE_LIVE' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (window close)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE' ORDER BY window_end_ms

panels.title: Live Metric Values
panels.description: The live counter upserts one Postgres row per pipeline under a fixed 1970-01-01 sentinel (see LIVE_WINDOW_MARKER in DeploymentFrequencyOperator) — there's no per-row window_start/window_end to select, and a wall-clock-bucketed approximation of one was actively misleading (it doesn't reflect each pipeline's own event-time window, which only LiveDeployCounter's internal state actually knows). resets_after instead just shows the configured live-window duration (FlinkConfig.DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_WINDOW, driven by the $deployment_frequency_window_seconds variable above — currently 1 day): each pipeline's count covers up to that much event-time and resets to 0 once the job-global watermark passes that far beyond this pipeline's own last reset point — not a fixed calendar boundary shared across pipelines. See the Window History panel below for real, per-row window boundaries.

targets.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (metric_type, pipeline_id) inserted_at AS "time", metric_type, pipeline_id, service_name, value, performance_band, ($deployment_frequency_window_seconds || ' seconds')::interval AS resets_after FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_LIVE' ORDER BY metric_type, pipeline_id, inserted_at DESC

panels.title: Deployment Frequency — Window History
panels.description: window_alive_until = window_end + ALLOWED_LATENESS: how long (in watermark time, not event time) this window's state stays open for late corrections after it first fires. It does NOT extend which event_timestamps belong to this window — that's always [window_start, window_end), for on-time and late events alike. is_window_closed compares window_alive_until against the actual job-global watermark (same value as the Current Watermark panel above, joined live) rather than wall-clock now() — true once that watermark has passed window_alive_until, meaning no more late corrections are possible and this row is final. To test truly-late handling: push an event timestamped inside [window_start, window_end) only after is_window_closed reads true for this row.

targets.rawSql: WITH wm AS (SELECT value AS watermark_ms FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'WATERMARK' AND pipeline_id = 'GLOBAL' ORDER BY inserted_at DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT to_timestamp(m.window_start_ms / 1000) AS window_start, to_timestamp(m.window_end_ms / 1000) AS window_end, m.pipeline_id, m.service_name, m.value AS deploys_per_day, m.sample_count AS deploy_count, m.inserted_at AS computed_at, to_timestamp(m.window_end_ms / 1000) + interval '$allowed_lateness_hours hours' AS window_alive_until, COALESCE(wm.watermark_ms > (m.window_end_ms + $allowed_lateness_hours * 3600000), false) AS is_window_closed FROM cicd_metrics m LEFT JOIN wm ON true WHERE m.metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY' ORDER BY m.window_end_ms DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Truly-Late Events — All Metrics (per event detail)
panels.description: Every event that missed its metric's allowed-lateness grace period, across all three windowed metrics that side-output truly-late data (DeploymentFrequencyOperator, DoraOperators.changeFailureRate, PipelineHealthOperator) — see TrulyLateAuditOperator. source_metric identifies which metric's window the event was too late for; it's the same underlying cicd_alerts LATE_EVENT audit trail regardless of event_type, so use source_metric (not event_type) to filter by metric. reason is computed here from event_time vs watermark_time (not stored by the job) — a one-line summary of how far behind the watermark the event was when it arrived.

targets.rawSql: SELECT inserted_at AS computed_at, payload->>'source_metric' AS source_metric, payload->>'event_id' AS event_id, payload->>'pipeline_id' AS pipeline_id, payload->>'service_name' AS service_name, payload->>'event_type' AS event_type, payload->>'event_time' AS event_time, payload->>'watermark_time' AS watermark_time, CASE WHEN payload->>'watermark_time' IS NULL THEN 'No watermark had been reported yet when this event was audited' ELSE 'Arrived ' || ((payload->>'watermark_time')::timestamptz - (payload->>'event_time')::timestamptz)::text || ' behind the watermark — past this window''s allowed-lateness grace period' END AS reason FROM cicd_alerts WHERE alert_type = 'LATE_EVENT' ORDER BY inserted_at DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Flink Processing Latency Trend Analysis (ms, avg per minute)
panels.description: Flink's own processing latency: inserted_at - flink_received_at, per metric_type, bucketed by minute. flink_received_at is the wall-clock time CicdEventDeserializer deserialised the record (System.currentTimeMillis()) — see SourceTiming.earliest() for how it's chosen when a metric result folds multiple events. Unlike a Kafka-CreateTime-based measure, this excludes consumer lag/backlog catch-up time, isolating deserialize -> window/compute -> sink latency. Plotted by inserted_at (real wall-clock arrival time, not event time) since this measures pipeline throughput/lag, not a business metric — unlike the DORA panels above, a real-time X-axis is correct here. Rows with flink_received_at IS NULL (unset, see PostgresMetricSink) are excluded rather than shown as a bogus multi-decade latency.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('minute', inserted_at) AS "time", AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (inserted_at - flink_received_at)) * 1000) AS value, metric_type AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE flink_received_at IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) GROUP BY 1, metric_type ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Job Completed At (per metric type)
panels.description: MAX(inserted_at) per metric_type in the selected time range, excluding PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE/_LIVE/_LATE_EVENTS — the most recent moment Flink wrote a result of each type. No single automatic e2e-latency figure here: pairing this against a 'first event pushed' reference reliably requires the producer to mark push boundaries itself (timing-gap heuristics on the Flink side can't tell a real pause between two pushes apart from a same-push stall caused by consumer lag/backpressure). generate_load_test_events.py now prints the wall-clock time it starts pushing a batch — compare that manually against this table for e2e latency.

targets.rawSql: SELECT metric_type, to_char(MAX(inserted_at) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"') AS max_inserted_at FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type NOT IN ('PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE', 'PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE_LIVE', 'PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE_LATE_EVENTS') AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) GROUP BY metric_type ORDER BY MAX(inserted_at) DESC

panels.title: Flink Processing Latency (ms, latest row per metric type)
panels.description: For each metric_type, its most-recently-inserted row's own (inserted_at - flink_received_at) — not an average across a bucket like Panel 11. flink_received_at is the wall-clock time CicdEventDeserializer deserialised the record (System.currentTimeMillis()); for paired/windowed metric types it's the EARLIEST contributing event's receive time (see SourceTiming.earliest()), so this is pure engine+write latency for *_LIVE/WATERMARK, but includes real business-process/window-close wait for LEAD_TIME_FOR_CHANGES/CHANGE_FAILURE_RATE/MEAN_TIME_TO_RECOVERY/DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY/PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE — don't compare those two groups directly. Rows with flink_received_at IS NULL (unset, see PostgresMetricSink) are excluded rather than shown as a bogus multi-decade latency.

targets.rawSql: SELECT metric_type, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (inserted_at - flink_received_at)) * 1000 AS latency_ms FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (metric_type) metric_type, inserted_at, flink_received_at FROM cicd_metrics WHERE flink_received_at IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY metric_type, inserted_at DESC) latest ORDER BY latency_ms DESC

_disabledPanels_readme: Panels below are not part of the active 'panels' array (Grafana ignores this key) — kept here so they're easy to restore. Move a panel object back into 'panels' to re-enable it.

_disabledPanels.title: Deployment Frequency — Truly-Late Events (count per window)
_disabledPanels._disabledReason: Backing metric (DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_LATE_EVENTS) is no longer sunk — LateEventOperator wiring commented out in PipelineObservabilityJob.java (see [C] there). Its processing-time 10-min window rarely closed before the job restarted, leaving this permanently on 'No data'. Live metrics, Window History, and the per-event detail panel above are unaffected.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_timestamp(window_start_ms / 1000) AS window_start, to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS window_end, pipeline_id, service_name, value AS late_event_count, inserted_at AS computed_at FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_LATE_EVENTS' ORDER BY window_end_ms DESC LIMIT 20
